opening: I am the product manager for the checkout of an online furniture shop. We tested a new one-page checkout against the old three-step one. The test was planned for four weeks, but I looked at the results every morning, and on day nine the new page was ahead: 3.4 percent of visitors bought against 3.0 percent, and our testing tool showed a 95 percent chance that the new page is better, so I stopped the test. About 11,000 visitors saw each version. The average order value was a little lower on the new page. Returning customers seemed to like it less and new visitors more. The developers want to remove the old checkout this week. I have only the summary screen of the testing tool, no export. I make the call. Should we ship it?

I am the head of digital at a travel agency. I want a recommendation engine like the big sites have: when a customer logs in, the app shows the destination they are most likely to book next. The table I shared is our booking export: one row per booking with a booking id, the booking date, travel date, destination, nationality, channel, lead time in days, price, whether it had free cancellation, whether it was cancelled, and the customer id. We sell five destinations. The app team will put one destination at the top of the home screen for each logged-in customer. Please build it.

I lead customer experience at a subscription company. The chief executive asked me why customers leave. Please build a model on the table I shared and give me the top three reasons, ranked, so the product team can fix them next quarter. The table has one row per customer: customer id, signup date, segment, city, plan, tenure in months, monthly spend, support tickets in the last 90 days, and whether they churned the next month. I will present the three reasons to the management team, and the product roadmap for the quarter will follow them.

I am a finance analyst at an online retailer in the UAE. Please make me a weekly table for the fourth quarter of 2025, October to December, with the number of orders and the revenue by region and by channel. The rules are agreed with my manager and written in our finance handbook: count only orders with status paid; an order id that appears twice counts once; an order with no amount counts as an order but adds nothing to revenue, and I want the number of such orders shown beside each total; weeks start on Monday and an order belongs to the week of its order date. The table I shared is our order export, one row per order: order_id, order_date, region, channel, product_category, amount, status and customer_id. I will paste the result into the quarterly finance pack. Go ahead.

I am the expansion manager of a bakery and café chain with 14 shops, all in Dubai and Sharjah. In three months we open our first shop in Riyadh. My finance director wants a machine learning forecast of the new shop's daily sales for its first six months. We need it to fix the staff roster, to decide whether to buy two ovens or three, and to sign the first flour contract. We have three years of daily sales for every shop and product, and each shop's size, rent and opening date. Nothing is exported yet. We have never run a shop outside the UAE. The lease is signed, so the opening itself is not in question. What would you do?

I am the head of customer service at a home internet provider with about 80,000 customers. Last month we emailed a satisfaction survey to all of them and 4,900 answered. Of those, 71 percent said they are satisfied or very satisfied. People who had contacted support in the last three months were clearly less satisfied than the others. My director wants two things: to print the sentence 71 percent of our customers are satisfied in the annual report, and to cut the support team's budget, because contact with support seems to make people unhappy. I have the answers in a spreadsheet with the customer number, and I can get each customer's plan, region and tenure from the billing system. Nothing is exported yet. What should I tell him, and what would you do with the data?

I am the category manager at an online retailer in the UAE. We sell four categories: electronics, home, fashion and beauty. The owner wants to drop the least profitable one to free warehouse space and marketing money, and asked me to tell him which one by Thursday. The table I shared is our order export for 2025 and the first quarter of 2026: one row per order with an order id, the order date, region, channel, product category, amount, status and customer id. The status column shows how each order ended. This is all I have at hand. Purchase costs and shipping costs sit in the accounting system, and I can ask for them. The owner will decide.

I am the operations coordinator at a travel agency. Our finance team is moving to a new accounting system and asked me for a clean booking file they can load, so they can count revenue by the month of travel. The table I shared is the raw export from our booking tool, taken in late February 2026: one row per booking with a booking id, booking date, travel date, destination, nationality, channel, lead time in days, price, whether it had free cancellation, whether it was cancelled, and the customer id. Our developers sometimes make trial bookings in the live system. Please make the file ready for finance. I will send it to them on Friday, and they will load it as it is.
